summary: Build mode (B): log cabins, windows, doors, palisade forts and chimneys from the logs and stone in the pack (scripts/building/). Every number here is a design value and tunable. Pieces are 3 m modules: they snap to each other's sockets (floor edges, wall ends and tops, roof ends, wall faces) or stand on the ground on a 0.25 m / 15 degree grid.
provenance: Pieces, meshes and colliders are the project's own, generated in code (scripts/building/build_geometry.gd) with the fort's StructureMeshKit and StructureMaterials (the CC0 Poly Haven textures processed for the fort, assets/environment/structures/textures/SOURCES.md). No animation data is used.

opening_repair.name: Repair the wall
opening_repair.summary: Aimed into an opening chopped in the palisade or the gate (WallCuts): the logs (or planks) stand there again.

opening_cover.name: Cover with logs
opening_cover.summary: Aimed into an opening chopped in the palisade or the gate: horizontal logs across it close it (the axe chops them out again).

opening_door.name: Door in the wall
opening_door.summary: Aimed into an opening in the palisade chopped open from the ground up (1.85 m): a hung plank door, E opens and shuts it.

floor.name: Floor and foundation
floor.summary: A 3 x 3 m puncheon floor on hewn sills over a dry-laid fieldstone footing (up to 1 m of slope under it).

wall.name: Notched log wall
wall.summary: Nine courses of round logs hewn flat on the faces, clay chinking, saddle-notched where two walls meet.

wall_window.name: Log wall with window
wall_window.summary: A log wall with a cased window and board shutters.

wall_door.name: Log wall with door
wall_door.summary: A log wall with a cased doorway and a hung plank door (E opens and shuts it).

post.name: Corner post
post.summary: A hewn post for a floor corner or a wall end (post-and-log corners).

gable.name: Gable end
gable.summary: A board-clad gable on top of a wall, under the roof's pitch.

roof.name: Roof
roof.summary: One 3 m bay of riven-shingle roof on the tops of two walls; bays join along the ridge.

hearth.name: Stone hearth and chimney
hearth.summary: A fieldstone firebox and stack, built against a wall (inside or out) or on its own. E lays firewood in it and lights it: a fire indoors that warms the whole cabin under its roof, cooks (F) and sends its smoke up the chimney.

campfire.name: Campfire
campfire.summary: A ring of fieldstones round a laid fire of split wood. E lights it (flint and steel, or a lit torch), feeds it firewood, or smothers it; it lights and warms the camp and keeps wolves off.

lean_to.name: Brush lean-to
lean_to.summary: Two forked posts, a ridge pole and a slope of poles thatched with brush and bark, open on one side to face a fire.

palisade.name: Palisade wall
palisade.summary: Eight sharpened stakes set in the ground (they follow it), with a ribband pinned inside.

palisade_gate.name: Palisade gate
palisade_gate.summary: Two hewn gate posts, a lintel and two plank leaves (E opens and shuts them).

bough_bed.name: Bough bed
bough_bed.summary: Hemlock and balsam boughs laid thick and shingled butt-down between two side logs, off the cold ground. E (or Z on it) sleeps in it: warmer, and a better sleep (the core's bough bed).

drying_rack.name: Drying rack
drying_rack.summary: A pole scaffold to stand beside a campfire: venison cut in thin strips and hung over the slow, smoky fire dries to jerky in one or two game days (E hangs it, E takes the jerky down).

woodpile.name: Woodpile
woodpile.summary: Two poles on the ground between end stakes. E stacks the pack's firewood on it (up to 18). Within 3 m of a campfire or a hearth it feeds the fire by itself as it burns down, through the night.

smokehouse.name: Smokehouse
smokehouse.summary: A small bark-walled hut with a smudge fire in its floor: a larder that keeps your food and jerky (E), and smokes the raw venison in it into jerky in a game day while the smudge smoulders (firewood: 4 game hours a stick; a woodpile beside it feeds it).

pole_bed.name: Pole bed
pole_bed.summary: A frame of poles on four short legs, a straw tick and a deer hide over it: the best sleep off the ground (E or Z on it).

musket_rack.name: Musket rack
musket_rack.summary: Two posts, a notched rail and a butt trough: six long guns or bows stand in it, loaded as they were (hold E with one in the hands to stand it there; E takes it again).

spear_barrel.name: Spear barrel
spear_barrel.summary: A coopered barrel with its head knocked in: five spears, dart throwers or muskets stand in it (hold E to stand one there; E takes it).

tanning_frame.name: Tanning frame
tanning_frame.summary: A fleshing beam and a pole frame to lace a hide in. E works a deer hide: scraped into rawhide, or with brains (or cornmeal) worked in and smoked over a lit fire beside it, dressed into soft buckskin.

alchemy_table.name: Alchemy table
alchemy_table.summary: An herbalist's bench: mortar and pestle, crocks, a stoppered bottle, herbs hung to dry. E makes remedies from what you forage: plantain salve, wintergreen tea (by a lit fire), ginseng tonic.

workbench.name: Workbench
workbench.summary: A heavy plank bench on splayed legs, an awl, a knife and a mallet on it. E makes moccasins and fur mitts (buckskin, pelts, sinew) and mends worn moccasins, and cuts arrows, throwing spears and atlatl darts from branches, poles and flint.

stretching_hoop.name: Stretching hoop
stretching_hoop.summary: A bent-sapling hoop on a stake. E laces a wolf or fox pelt into it, fleshed; it dries on the hoop in two or three game days, graded better for the stretching, and E takes it down.

work_stone.name: Knapping stone
work_stone.summary: A flat-topped boulder to work on, with a hammerstone: the first tools from nothing. E: a flint knife (chert knapped into a blade and hafted), a stone axe (a chert head lashed into a pole), a bow drill for fire, cord twisted from elm bark. Chert nodules lie in the hollows, poles and sticks in the woods.

charcoal_mound.name: Charcoal mound
charcoal_mound.summary: Firewood stacked on end and covered with earth and turf, lit and left to char slowly for about a game day: charcoal for the forge. E lights it (a lit torch, a bow drill or flint and steel), then takes the charcoal out when it is done.

forge.name: Forge
forge.summary: A bloomery forge: a fieldstone hearth with a clay-lined smelting shaft, bag bellows of rawhide and a stone anvil on a stump. Charcoal and bog iron ore smelt into bar iron; bar iron is forged into axes, knives, a mattock, a tomahawk, flint and steel, steel traps, a bullet mould and fish hooks.

trap_steel.name: Steel trap
trap_steel.summary: A long-spring steel trap staked on a run. Place it, then E sets it (a steel trap from the pack; the Trapping and Fishing check). Each dawn it may hold a fox, a wolf, a raccoon, a mink, a marten or a fisher: E takes and skins the catch and sets it again. By water or along thick cover it takes more; near the camp or after gunfire less. Taken down, the trap comes back.

trap_snare.name: Spring-pole snare
trap_snare.summary: A sapling bent over a run and a cord noose on a trigger peg. Place it among young trees, then E sets it (cordage from the pack). It takes hares, now and then a fox or a raccoon.

trap_deadfall.name: Deadfall
trap_deadfall.summary: A log propped over the bait on a figure-four between two stakes. Place it, then E sets it (deadfall stakes from the pack, and a hatchet or an axe). Raccoons, martens, minks, fishers and hares.

storage_chest.name: Storage chest
storage_chest.summary: A plank chest with iron straps and a hasp. E opens it: put things from the pack in it and take them out again. What is in it is kept in the save.

take_down.name: Take down
take_down.summary: Takes a piece down again: part of its cost comes back (half at Novice, three quarters at Master).
